text:
anne (design): quick design review — small set of UX nits on the Compliance panel: retention dropdown, region fallback copy, and KMS/encryption badges. sharing a mock: https://files.redwood/mockups/retention-region-v3.png

sam (engineering): looks good. two questions: 1) if a region is temporarily unavailable, do we show a fallback region in the dropdown? 2) what should the default selection be for new orgs?

anne (design): good calls. proposal: keep the dropdown ordered by proximity, but show a decorated fallback item like: 'eu-west1 — fallback (auto)' with info icon. default for new orgs = 'Auto (closest region)'. avoids accidental data locality assumptions.

kevin (devex): +1 to fallback label. copy nit: currently the badge says "Customer key" vs "Redwood key" — can we make it explicit: "Customer‑managed KMS" and "Redwood‑managed key"? helps support + audits. also prefer Title Case for badges? open to debate.

maya (product): Legal asked that we avoid implying key ownership transfer. maybe: "Customer-managed (KMS)" and "Managed by Redwood". also we should surface the KMS provider when available (e.g., 'AWS KMS — key-id').

security-bot: NOTE: Policy 3.2 requires display of key scope and owner for any exportable audit logs. Ensure UI renders key-id or a reference token, not the secret itself.

sam (engineering): for the audit log copy, current entry: 
```
User maya changed encryption from customer to redwood
```
I want to change that to a single-line structured sentence with region + key reference. e.g.:
```
[2026-03-01 14:22:03] maya@acme updated retention: 30d → 90d (region: eu-west1, encryption: Customer‑managed KMS/CUST_KMS_US-EU)
```
Thoughts?

anne (design): that structured format is good. two UX points: 1) shorten long key tokens with ellipsis and tooltip on hover. 2) make the phrase accessible for screen readers — avoid punctuation-heavy tokens where possible.

kevin (devex): agree on ellipsis + tooltip. copy tweak: replace 'Customer‑managed KMS/CUST_KMS_US-EU' with 'Customer-managed KMS (CUST_KMS…)' so the primary readable label comes first. also recommend consistent capitalization: 'Customer‑managed KMS' vs 'customer-managed' elsewhere.

maya (product): for the retention dropdown help text, proposed copy: "Retention period controls how long generated data (requests, responses, telemetry) is stored. Choose a region to keep data in that jurisdiction."
Could we add a small clarifying sentence: "If your selected region becomes unavailable, Redwood may route to the nearest region to maintain availability — we will record this in the audit log."

anne (design): i like that. a11y note: the help text must be linked via aria-describedby on the dropdown so screen readers read the clarification before choices. Also ensure focus state for the region badge is visible (current 1.4:1 contrast fails).

sam (engineering): technical constraint: when a fallback happens we only have the fallback region id, not the original desired region, so the audit log should record both: intended_region and served_region when possible. suggestion for UI: show a toast when fallback occurs: "Serving from us-east1 due to eu-west1 capacity — recorded in audit log." small and actionable.

kevin (devex): copy for that toast: "Serving from us-east1 (fallback). See audit log for details." keep it short. please add :warning: only if data residency risk exists.

maya (product): final pass on badges and audit copy: 1) Badge text: 'Customer-managed KMS' / 'Redwood-managed' 2) Audit log entry example: 
```
[2026-03-01 14:22:03] maya@acme changed retention: 30d → 90d; intended_region=eu-west1; served_region=us-east1; encryption="Customer-managed KMS (CUST_KMS…)"
```
make sure quotes are present around the encryption token.

anne (design): i'll update the mock and push a11y changes: stronger focus ring, color adjustments for badge contrast, aria-describedby on dropdown/help. will also add a tooltip pattern for truncated key IDs.

sam (engineering): i'll wire up the audit log format and the fallback toast. i'll also add a feature flag for the toast copy so we can test legal wording with a small cohort.

kevin (devex): once anne pushes the updated mock, can we do a quick copy pass? i'll check capitalization & microcopy consistency across console and audit exports.

maya (product): sounds good. timeline: anne — mock updates by EOD Wednesday; sam — implementation + flag the following week; kevin — copy pass after mock. thanks all :thumbsup:

anne (design): thanks — i'll drop the updated PNG and a11y checklist in this thread when done. :sparkles:
